state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Firstly, great job identifying the negative-sloping section on the graph! Remember, on a distance-time graph, a negative slope indicates that the object is moving away from its starting point. In this case, Fido might be running away from home during that part of the graph. Can you explain why you thought he had fallen asleep?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought Fido might have fallen asleep because the line goes down, and I thought that meant he wasn't moving. But if it's showing he's moving away from home, does that mean he's actually running back towards it when the line goes back up? I'm still a bit confused about how to tell the difference between resting and moving on these graphs.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's clarify the concept of rest and movement on a distance-time graph. When the line goes down, it means the object is moving away from its starting point. When the line goes back up, it means the object is moving towards its starting point. So, in this case, Fido is not resting when the line goes back up, but rather running back towards home. Can you see the difference now?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming negative slope means moving away when it actually means returning home), fails to engage the student's specific confusion about horizontal sections representing rest, and simply tells answers rather than scaffolding understanding, with the student remaining confused by Turn 2.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses some explanation but makes a critical mathematical error (stating negative slope means moving away when it actually means returning home), lacks worked examples, and relies heavily on questioning rather than direct traditional instruction.
